scenes.tts: They alternated whose name came first on the papers, to signal that the work was exactly equal. Stanford Moore and William Stein argued every sentence until a finding was vetted to perfection, and a colleague described them as a single intellectual entity.

scenes.tts: Their automated analyzer used synthetic resins to separate the amino acids, then detected each one through a color-changing ninhydrin reaction, and that machine decoded ribonuclease, an enzyme of 124 amino acids — the first enzyme read end to end.

scenes.tts: Moore compared a protein's sequence to a coded message that dictates the three-dimensional shape and function of the biological machine, and now they could read it.

scenes.tts: Then the bodies of both men failed them and neither stopped. Guillain-Barré left Stein quadriplegic; he kept guiding his lab and editing manuscripts with gracious detail, hosting seminars from his apartment.
scenes.visual: both failed; Stein quadriplegic, kept working
scenes.narration: Then the bodies of both men failed them and neither stopped. Guillain-Barré left Stein quadriplegic; he kept guiding his lab and editing manuscripts with gracious detail, hosting seminars from his apartment.

scenes.tts: ALS took Moore's hands — the same hands that once machined solenoid valves and tuned gear-driven turntables now resting in his lap with an unwilling stillness — while in the lab a pen recorder traced peaks of a molecular logic he could no longer physically touch. He lived by his own quiet mantra: the investigator does not usually move from discovery to discovery; he moves from problem to problem.
